claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To begin, I need to understand the situation with your child or children.

**How old is the child (or children) you're claiming for?** 

Please tell me:
- The child's name and age, or
- If you have multiple children, their names and ages

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation. Child Benefit has different requirements depending on whether the child is:
- **Under 16** (different rules apply)
- **16-19 years old** (need to check education/training status)
- **20 or over** (may not be eligible)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hi! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit and wanted to check if I'm eligible.

I have one child - Alex, who's 17 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, **Alex, who is 17 years old**.

Since Alex is 17, they fall into the **16-19 age group**, which means I need to check their education or training status to determine eligibility.

Let me navigate to the next question:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to understand **Alex's current situation regarding education or training**:

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In education or training** (e.g., school, college, university, apprenticeship, or other approved training)?
2. **Recently left education** (within the last 20 weeks) and potentially eligible for an extension?
3. **Neither** - not in education/training and hasn't recently left?

Please let me know which applies to Alex's situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is currently in education - he's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! So **Alex is currently in education at sixth form college studying for A-levels**.

Since Alex is in education, I need to check the level of education to ensure it meets the eligibility requirements.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! I can see that Alex's A-levels qualify as **approved education** for Child Benefit purposes. A-levels are on the list of approved qualifications.

However, I need to check a couple more things to confirm full eligibility:

**1. Study hours:** How many hours per week is Alex studying? (It needs to be at least 12 hours per week of supervised study for it to count as full-time education)

**2. Work status:** Is Alex working full-time (30+ hours per week), or does he only have part-time or no work commitments?

Please let me know about these two points.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Alex is studying full-time - definitely more than 12 hours a week with all his classes and coursework.

As for work, no, he doesn't work at all. He's focused on his studies.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! That's very helpful. So **Alex is studying full-time (well over 12 hours per week) and is not working**.

Let me navigate to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Since Alex is **not working at all**, this check is satisfied. He's working less than 24 hours per week.

Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check: **Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right, such as:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit

Or is he not receiving any of these benefits?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own right. He's just a student living at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! So **Alex is not receiving any benefits in his own right**.

Let me continue to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check: **Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Since he's studying A-levels at sixth form college, I want to confirm that he's **not in any form of apprenticeship** (such as an Intermediate, Advanced, or Degree Apprenticeship in England, or a Modern Apprenticeship in Scotland, etc.).

Is that correct - Alex is not in any apprenticeship?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's correct - Alex is not in an apprenticeship. He's just doing his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! So **Alex is not in an apprenticeship** - he's purely studying A-levels at sixth form college.

Now let me move to the next important check, which is about your residency:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your residency status. To determine if you meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit, I need to understand which of the following applies to you:

**Do you:**
1. **Normally live in the UK** (this is the standard requirement)?
   
   OR are you in one of these specific situations:
2. Have **settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**?
3. Have **pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** (if so, we'd need to check additional criteria about work, study, or resources)?
4. Work **abroad as a Crown servant** in certain qualifying countries?

Which of these best describes your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK. I live in Manchester with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! So **you normally live in the UK in Manchester with Alex**.

That satisfies the residency requirement. Let me continue to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to confirm: **Are you responsible for Alex?**

This means one or more of the following:
1. **You live with Alex** (which you've already mentioned - you live together in Manchester), OR
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** (food, clothes, housing, pocket money, presents, etc.), OR
3. **You pay maintenance** under a court order or agreement

Since you've already told me you live with Alex in Manchester, this requirement is clearly satisfied. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check: **Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has any other person claimed it for him?**

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for each child. So I need to know:
- Is anyone else (such as Alex's other parent, a grandparent, or guardian) currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?
- Or have you and another person agreed that you should be the one to claim?

What's the situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me - I'm his parent and he lives with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! So **you are the only person claiming Child Benefit for Alex** - there's no other claimant.

Let me continue to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's living situation: **Is Alex currently:**
1. **In hospital**?
2. **In care** (local authority care)?
3. **Fostered** with a foster family?
4. **Living normally** at home with you?

Which applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is living normally at home with me in Manchester. He's not in hospital, care, or fostered - just a regular teenager living at home while he does his A-levels.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! So **Alex is living normally at home with you in Manchester**.

Let me continue to the final check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! One final check: **Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you personally paying for Alex's living expenses (housing, food, etc.), or is the council providing financial support for his accommodation or upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm paying for everything myself - the council isn't paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance at all. It's just me providing for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! That's the final piece of information I need. **You are paying for everything yourself, and the council is not contributing to Alex's accommodation or maintenance.**

You have now met all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit! Let me confirm your eligibility:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Now let me provide you with your final eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **You ARE ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex!**

### Summary:

**Child:** Alex (17 years old)

**Result:** ✅ **ELIGIBLE**

### Why You're Eligible:

✓ **Alex is a qualifying child** - He's 17 years old and in full-time approved education (A-levels at sixth form college)
✓ **Alex meets education requirements** - A-levels are approved qualifications and he's studying more than 12 hours per week
✓ **No disqualifying factors** - Alex doesn't work full-time, isn't receiving benefits, and isn't in a disqualifying apprenticeship
✓ **You meet claimant requirements** - You normally live in the UK (Manchester), you're responsible for Alex (living with him), you're the sole claimant, and you're paying for his accommodation and maintenance

---

### **Next Steps - How to Claim:**

1. **Apply online** at [www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim) or by post using **form CH2**

2. **Gather required documents:**
   - Proof of your identity (passport, driving licence, etc.)
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate
   - Proof of identity for Alex

3. **Important note:** If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, be aware of the **High Income Child Benefit Charge** - you may still be eligible but may have to pay back some of the benefit through tax

4. **Payment schedule:** Child Benefit is typically paid every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain other benefits)

If you have any other questions or need further clarification, feel free to ask!
